I've got a bit of a BI background, and yeah, unfortunately it would take a bit of effort to make it work well.

Basically every subverse would need to be tagged with specific and consistent identifiers and those tags would need to have weight assigned on a subverse by subverse basis. To be truly relevant the tag weights would need to be fluid based on the content of the subverse too. Then there would need to be an algorithm produced which calculates which subverses you're likely to like based on the tags (and their weighted values) associated with the subverses you're subscribed to, and which you're actively posting on.

To give you a real world example of how hard it would be to get good, look at the targeted ads that Google send to you versus those that Facebook send. Google is able to use your web browsing history, Gmail content, and search history to target the ads which is why they're generally pretty good. Facebook on the other hand relies only on what you post, what your friends post, and what you tell them you like, which results in some completely mismatched ads. Bing VS Google, and Hotmail VS Gmail are other good examples.

That being said I think its a great idea and would love to see it implemented one day.
